newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Commodities see coffee extend gain, gold weak.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Commodities see coffee extend gain, gold weak.

text.p: World coffee prices extended a rally on Wednesday when speculators piled in to the markets on news of a lower-than-expected rise in consumer coffee stocks and reports of a planned national strike in Brazil's ports.
Other commodity markets saw gold continue to slide, while oil was weaker and wheat retreated from six-month highs seen on Monday.

The Green Coffee Association reported after the close of New York trading on Tuesday that supplies of green coffee stored in U.S warehouses rose in March by 111,000 60-kg bags to 1,657,000 bags, versus analysts' forecasts of a build of between 250,000 and 300,000 bags.

Bullish sentiment was fuelled by news that Brazilian stevedores planned to go on national strike in sympathy with their colleagues at the key Brazilian port of Santos, who began an indefinite strike on Tuesday.
"The (national) strike will start at 0700 local (1000GMT) and last for two days," said Ernani Duarte, secretary-general of the National Stevedores' Union.
The national strike would represent the second stoppage in two weeks in Brazil, the world's number one coffee producer.

Robusta coffee futures for May were trading around $37 higher at $1,615 per tonne in London's Wednesday afternoon. New York futures for the arabica type of beans hit life of contract highs at $2.10 per pound in early trading.
Gold came under sustained pressure following on from a Tuesday sell-off and traders said further losses were seen ahead.
But analysts said the market's subsequent slight recovery from the day's low at $338 per ounce suggested it could be in for a period of consolidation before testing lower levels.
A fall in U.S housing starts intensified bearish sentiment weighing on gold, which was already depressed by Friday's higher-than-expected U.S. March producer price inflation data.

Crude oil prices for benchmark North Sea Brent Blend dropped to a new session low after U.S Department of Energy data released on Wednesday showed a rise of 2.6 million barrels in crude oil stocks. American Petroleum Institute figures issued on Tuesday showed a similar build in stocks.
The June Brent futures contract fell below $18 a barrel in London's Wednesday afternoon, before creeping up again.
Meanwhile copper and aluminium suffered falls on Wednesday as copper saw sharp selling in London's afternoon and dragged aluminium down with it.
Wheat continued its retreat after Monday's surge, while cocoa was weaker but off the day's lows.
